title: Evaluation and connected components of lisse condensed sheaves
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $D(T,\Lambda)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_T)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with ordinary derived tensor and unit $\Lambda_T[0]$, and $D_{\mathrm{lis}}(T,\Lambda)$ for its full subcategory of dualizable objects (objects admitting evaluation and coevaluation satisfying both triangle identities). For a profinite set $S$, use the analogous notation for sheaves on profinite sets over $S$, with finite jointly surjective covering families and coefficient ring the restriction of $\Lambda$ to that site. Let $T$ be a w-contractible affine scheme [sk-def-pe-wlocal], or an extremally disconnected profinite set, and put $A_T=\Gamma(T,\Lambda_T)$. A complex in $D(A_T)$ is perfect if it is represented by a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. The exact symmetric monoidal functor
$$F_T:D(A_T)\longrightarrow D(T,\Lambda),\qquad Q\longmapsto\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline {A_T}}\underline Q$$
uses constant sheaves with discrete coefficients [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor] and the constant-section map. It is fully faithful; its restriction induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Perf}(A_T)\simeq D_{\mathrm{lis}}(T,\Lambda)$ with inverse $R\Gamma(T,-)$.

For w-contractible affine $T$, put $S=\pi_0(T)$ with its quotient topology [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite]. There is a coefficient-compatible map of sites $\pi_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to S_{\mathrm{proet}}$, whose inverse image is induced by $S'\mapsto T\times_S S'$ (the inverse limit of the finite clopen subdivisions defining the profinite $S$-set $S'$). It induces an exact symmetric monoidal equivalence
$$\pi_T^*:D_{\mathrm{lis}}(S,\Lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{\mathrm{lis}}(T,\Lambda),\qquad \pi_T^*\Lambda_S\cong\Lambda_T,$$
and $A_T\cong\Gamma(S,\Lambda)$. Both scalar realization functors commute with this inverse image. In particular, putting $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$, for $P\in D(R)$ the complex $\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$ is naturally $F_T(A_T\otimes_R^L P)$.

source.place: Section 3 equations (3.1)-(3.2), Remark 3.2; Lemma 4.1(1)-(2) and Proposition 4.3(3)

proof.text: Put $\mathcal O=\Lambda_T$ and $A=A_T$. For either of the two allowed kinds of $T$, [lem-zl-contractible-derived-sections-tensor] gives an exact, colimit-preserving module evaluation and its termwise unbounded derived functor $G=R\Gamma(T,-)$; in particular $G$ is strong symmetric monoidal. Thus its application to evaluation and coevaluation maps preserves both triangle identities. This uses the derived tensor comparison, not a claim that scalar realization is t-exact.

Use the global-sections geometric morphism to the one-point topos, equipped with the constant-section map $\underline A\to\mathcal O$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], $E(M)=\mathcal O\otimes_{\underline A}\underline M$ is left adjoint to $\Gamma(T,-)$ on modules. Its total left derived functor exists and is computed on K-flat complexes with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. It is exactly $F_T$: the constant realization is termwise exact by [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor]. Apply [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived], with the exact right functor of step 1, to obtain $F_T\dashv G$ with the derived underived unit and counit. The derived tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and $F_T(A)=\mathcal O$ give its strong symmetric monoidal structure. As a derived pullback $F_T$ is exact for distinguished triangles.

For a free $A$-module $A^{(I)}$, the unit $A^{(I)}\to\Gamma(T,E(A^{(I)}))$ is the identity after identifying both sides with $A^{(I)}$: $E(A)=\mathcal O$ and both functors preserve coproducts. For an arbitrary module take a presentation $A^{(J)}\to A^{(I)}\to M\to0$. Since $E$ preserves cokernels as a left adjoint and $\Gamma(T,-)$ is exact and preserves coproducts by [lem-zl-contractible-derived-sections-tensor], the same unit is an isomorphism for $M$. This is a natural comparison, as it is the adjunction unit, independent of the presentation.

source.place: Equation (3.2) at the terminal object; ordinary free-presentation calculation

proof.text: For arbitrary $Q\in D(A)$ choose a K-flat complex $P$ with flat terms representing it by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], applied on the one-object site. The comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] represents $F_T(Q)$ by $E(P)$. Termwise evaluation computes $G$ by step 1. Step 3 in each degree gives the chain isomorphism $P\to\Gamma(T,E(P))$; its compatibility with the differential is naturality of the unit. By the derived-adjunction normalization in step 2 this represents $Q\to GF_T(Q)$, so the derived unit is invertible. Consequently the adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(F_TQ,F_TQ')=\operatorname{Hom}(Q,GF_TQ')$ identifies the map induced by $F_T$ with composition by an invertible unit. This proves full faithfulness on all of $D(A)$.

source.place: Equation (3.2), Remark 3.2 and Lemma 4.1(1), unbounded unit comparison

proof.text:
For dualizable $M,N\in D(T,\Lambda)$, write $M^\vee$ for a chosen dual. The two triangle identities give mutually inverse transpositions
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O,M^\vee\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}N).$$
Explicitly send $f$ to coevaluation followed by $1\otimes f$ (using symmetry to order the factors); the inverse tensors with $M$ and evaluates its $M^\vee$ factor. Applying $G$, the unit and tensor isomorphisms of step 1 take these same formulas to those for $(GM,G(M^\vee))$. The adjunction of step 2 at $A$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O,Z)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(A,GZ)$. Therefore these transpositions give a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(GM,GN)$, and the explicit formulas show that it is the map induced by $G$. Thus $G$ is fully faithful on dualizable objects.

source.place: Lemma 4.1(2), the duality transposition after applying symmetric monoidal sections

proof.text: By [lem-zl-ring-derived-dualizable-perfect], the dualizable objects of $D(A)$ are exactly $\operatorname{Perf}(A)$. The two strong symmetric monoidal functors therefore restrict to $F_T:\operatorname{Perf}(A)\rightleftarrows D_{\mathrm{lis}}(T,\Lambda):G$. The unit is invertible by step 4. For dualizable $M$, the triangle identity gives $G(\epsilon_M)\eta_{GM}=1$, hence $G(\epsilon_M)=\eta_{GM}^{-1}$. Both $F_TGM$ and $M$ are dualizable, and full faithfulness of $G$ from step 5 reflects isomorphisms (lift the inverse and use faithfulness on both composites). Thus $\epsilon_M$ is invertible. The restricted unit and counit prove the claimed equivalence with inverse $R\Gamma(T,-)$.

source.place: Lemma 4.1(2); scalar dualizability is Stacks Tag 0FNS, lemma-have-dual-derived

proof.text: Now let $T$ be w-contractible affine and put $S=\pi_0(T)$. By [sk-def-pe-wlocal], $S$ is extremally disconnected. Apply [lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site] to obtain the specified component site morphism $\pi_T$ and $p_T\cong q_S\pi_T$. Inverse images of this factorization identify $\pi_T^{-1}\Lambda_S$ with $\Lambda_T$, preserving the constant sections. By [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact] this identified-coefficient module inverse image is exact. Its termwise derived functor $\pi_T^*$ is strong symmetric monoidal by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-point-basis-evaluation], applied with $X=T,U=T,F=\Lambda$, gives the natural ring isomorphism $A_T\cong\Gamma(S,\Lambda)$. The geometric w-contractibility hypothesis here implies the weak contractibility required in that evaluation statement by the covering-refinement theorem [det-pe-wcb-clopen-partition]: local lifts on a finite clopen partition glue to a section.

source.place: Equation (4.1), Proposition 4.3(3) and coefficient evaluation; clopen refinement is Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.4.9

proof.text:
Identify the two scalar rings by the canonical isomorphism of step 7 and call the result $A$. Inverse image preserves constant module sheaves, by composition of the constant geometric inverse image with $\pi_T^{-1}$. For a K-flat, flat-term representative $P$ over $A$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] computes both scalar realizations after this pullback. The coefficient identification and the tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] give naturally
$$\pi_T^* F_S(P)\cong\pi_T^*(\Lambda_S\otimes^L_{\underline A}\underline P)\cong\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline A}\underline P=F_T(P).$$
The comparison is induced by the identical constant sections and the map $p_T\cong q_S\pi_T$; its representative maps are natural in chain maps and invert quasi-isomorphisms. They descend naturally on $D(A)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. On perfect objects the two horizontal scalar functors are equivalences by step 6 for $S$ and $T$. Therefore this commuting square identifies $\pi_T^*$ on dualizable objects with the identity equivalence on $\operatorname{Perf}(A)$; it is the claimed exact symmetric monoidal equivalence, with $\pi_T^*\Lambda_S\cong\Lambda_T$.

source.place: Commutative square in the proof of Proposition 4.3(3), and Remark 3.2

proof.text:
For the final scalar formula let $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$ and choose a K-flat, flat-term $R$-complex $P$ representing the given object by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The ringed pullback result [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], first on the point site along $R\to A_T$ and then for the constant-section morphisms, says that $A_T\otimes_R P$ and the corresponding constant sheaf complexes are valid K-flat models. Hence the comparison in question is represented by the chain isomorphism
$$\Lambda_T\otimes_{\underline {A_T}}\underline{(A_T\otimes_R P)}\longrightarrow\Lambda_T\otimes_{\underline R}\underline P,\qquad b\otimes(a\otimes p)\longmapsto ba\otimes p.$$
Its inverse sends $b\otimes p$ to $b\otimes(1\otimes p)$; both are balanced, commute with $1\otimes d_P$, and commute with every map of representatives. Constants commute with the first scalar extension by [lem-sfb-constant-realization-derived-scalar-extension]. Localization of these K-flat models by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] proves the natural isomorphism $F_T(A_T\otimes_R^L P)\cong\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$ for all $P\in D(R)$.

source.place: Remark 3.2 and equations (3.1)–(3.2), associativity of scalar realization

proof_origin.place: Section 3 (3.1)–(3.2), Remark 3.2; Lemma 4.1(1)–(2), construction (4.1), proof of Proposition 4.3(3)
